correctness.rationale: At root e_j=ζ_d^j, the residue of dw/(w^d−1) is ζ_d^j/d, so the meridian period is (2πi/d)ζ_d^j. Any nonzero α=Σa_jζ_d^j of Σ|a_j|≤N is a cyclotomic integer with |Norm α|≥1. The two identity/conjugate embeddings contribute |α|², while each of the other q−2 embeddings is at most N, giving |α|≥N^{−(q−2)/2}. For q=φ(d)≥4, (L+1)^q pairwise distinct power sums lie in [-qL,qL]², and a cell pigeonhole collision with coefficient length≤qL yields |α|≤6√2 q L^{1−q/2}; L=⌊N/q⌋ plus small-N bound establishes the same exponent. When q=2, d=3,4,6 and all nonzero cyclotomic integers have modulus≥1, attained at 1. When q>2, arbitrarily small nonzero group elements plus multiplication by ζ_d produce two nonparallel real lines in the closure, hence density in C. The proof is not a finite computational extrapolation; source checker only illustrates small conductor budgets.
